title: Inverted full-back: 4-3-3 into 3-2-5
summary: Reds build up from a 4-3-3 that becomes a 3-2-5: the right-back steps inside next to the holding midfielder, the left-back tucks into a back three, and five forwards pin the Blues' 4-4-2 back line so the eights receive between the lines.

players.note: tucks in as left centre-back of a back three
inverted: steps into midfield beside the 6

principles.name: Inverted full-back forms a 2-man pivot
principles.statement: The right-back leaves the touchline and stands beside the holding midfielder, so the first pressing line of two cannot screen both pivots.
principles.visual_proof: H2 runs from the right touchline to a central slot next to H6 before the pass arrives

principles.name: Eights live in the half-spaces
principles.statement: The two eights stand in the half-spaces between the Blues' midfield and defensive lines, where neither line can reach them in time.
principles.visual_proof: H10 receives between A6 and A4 facing forward

principles.name: Five pin four
principles.statement: Five forwards across the last line pin the back four, so a defender stepping out leaves a man free behind him.
principles.visual_proof: the back four stays deep and H7 is free when A2 steps up

triggers.cue: A9 presses H4 and blocks the pass to H2
triggers.response: H4 lays the ball into H6, who turns to find H10 in the half-space

strengths.text: A 3+2 base gives five safe passing options against two strikers

weaknesses.text: If the pass into the pivot is intercepted the right flank is empty behind H2

counters.text: Blues' right midfielder jumps onto H2 early and the striker screens H6

assumptions: Blues defend in a compact mid-block and do not press the goalkeeper
